analysis: Examined three modified ProviderCore files. (1) ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift: unloadModel now calls selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue(now: .now) after a successful Nemotron Super retirement (head 1133-1137) and after a normal unload (head 1204). This only schedules recovery checks for waiting selected models at the next capacity tick. It does not change admission, eviction guards, KEK/cache handling, or encryption paths, and does not relax any memory or ownership gate. Early-return paths (failed GLM5 retirement, forEviction refusals) are untouched. (2) ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift: commitModelSelection tracks enabledModelsAtLastSwitch alongside hasPersistedModelSwitch. It is set only after stageReplacement succeeds (head 32) and restored in the rollback path with the persisted file (head 55). Residual: if stageReplacement or a later step throws before restore, the value was already updated, but the restore at line 55 only runs if persistedReplacement was set. The variable is set right after persistedReplacement, so the ordering is consistent; stageReplacement throwing leaves it unchanged. This is state consistency, not a security boundary. (3) ProviderLoop+ModelSwitch.swift: modelSwitchMutationsSettled now also requires selectedModelRecovery.attempt == nil (head 143). This tightens the drain barrier so a background recovery load cannot run concurrently with a switch. It is a conservative change. The possible availability side-effect is that a hung recovery attempt could keep the drain waiting until the deadline. That is bounded by the request timeout, or the nil-deadline path, which loops indefinitely; this is a minor liveness concern for the operator-initiated local CLI switch, not an adversary-reachable one (T-059 concerns the add-on hold, not this path). The definition and implementation of selectedModelRecovery (attempt, makeAllDue) are outside the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that attempt is cleared on cancellation or shutdown. No coordinator-facing, attestation, or provider key trust-boundary behavior changed. No findings.
